xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4299: security: Traefik template publishes 80/443/8080 on all interfaces, so LAN clients can mint a dashboard session via a forged Host header

plan.title: security: Traefik template publishes 80/443/8080 on all interfaces, so LAN clients can mint a dashboard session via a forged Host header
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The Traefik template publishes 80/443/8080 on every interface, and isLoopbackPeer trusts every Docker-bridge peer, which is what every Traefik-forwarded request is. A LAN client that sends Host: overdeck.localhost to https://<lan-ip>/api/dashboard/session gets a root overdeck_session cookie, and every uncredentialed /api/* call passes the remote request gate. This was reproduced on the planning host on 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 plus Set-Cookie, with Traefik logging source 192.168.1.64.
narratives.Proposal: Publish Traefik on 127.0.0.1 by default, with an explicit [traefik] bind = "all" opt-in. Migrate existing compose files through one helper (migrateTraefikCompose) that runs from pan install, pan sync, pan up (which recreates a running container on change), pan dev and startTraefikBody. In the dashboard, trust a Docker-bridge peer only when its rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry is loopback or a host Docker-bridge IP, so a LAN request through an exposed Traefik gets 401 from both the mint and the remote gate. pan doctor reports a container still published on all interfaces. Document the new posture in DASHBOARD-AUTH.md, docker-setup.mdx and DNS_SETUP.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No Traefik ipAllowList middleware (it answers 403, not the epic's 401, and duplicates the dashboard check)
- No change to api.insecure on :8080 beyond loopback binding
- No change to the in-container trust branch peerIsLocalContainerNetwork
- No change to literal-loopback peer trust behind Tailscale Serve or cloudflared (W-SEC4, PAN-4645, owns require_token_mint auto-enable)
- No defense against host-local containers that call the API directly with a self-set X-Forwarded-For (existing local-machine trust boundary)
- No rewrite of infra/wsl2hosts/sync-wsl2hosts.ps1
- No [::1] port bindings
- No automatic restart of the live overdeck-traefik container by the work agent
- No allowlist raise in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt

autoDecisions.summary: Default bind is 127.0.0.1 for every install, with no special case for WSL2
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for loopback as the default. Under the forwarded-client rule, a WSL2 Windows browser is a non-local client in both bind modes, so special-casing WSL2 would not restore its auto-mint.

autoDecisions.summary: LAN exposure is an explicit opt-in: [traefik] bind = "loopback" | "all" in config.toml
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says to make LAN exposure an explicit opt-in config key if that access is wanted. infra/wsl2hosts/sync-wsl2hosts.ps1 maps hostnames to the WSL VM IP, so some users do need non-loopback binding. An enum, not a free-form IP, keeps config from injecting text into the compose file.
A [::1] binding fails container start on hosts with IPv6 disabled. Browsers, curl and Node 22 fetch fall back from a refused ::1 to 127.0.0.1, and the DNS methods write 127.0.0.1.

autoDecisions.summary: The dashboard reads the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry for Docker-bridge peers only
autoDecisions.rationale: Traefik appends the client it saw, so the last entry cannot be forged. The planning probe showed LAN source 192.168.1.64 and local source 172.23.0.1 (the bridge gateway), so loopback-or-bridge-IP separates them. Literal-loopback proxies belong to W-SEC4.

autoDecisions.summary: The in-container trust branch stays unchanged
autoDecisions.rationale: Traefik's ingress gateway (172.23.0.0/16 on the planning host) is not on the overdeck network (192.168.48.0/20). Applying the rule inside UAT containers could re-break their session mint (PAN-1737). Loopback binding already closes their LAN path.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs are in scope despite the issue body's 'Docs: None'
autoDecisions.rationale: docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md names PAN-4299 under 'Does NOT defend', the original issue AC requires that section to change, and finalize requires a docs item.

autoDecisions.summary: Add a pan doctor check instead of auto-restarting Traefik on pan reload
autoDecisions.rationale: pan reload restarts only the dashboard. A doctor error with the fix 'pan restart --traefik' makes a stale exposed container visible without the CLI recreating the operator's proxy unasked.

metadata.sizeJustification: 20 files. The subsystem count of 9 is inflated because the lint counts each depth-2 doc file (docs/DASHBOARD-AUTH.md, docs/DNS_SETUP.md, guides/docker-setup.mdx) and each test root (tests/lib, tests/unit) as its own subsystem. The real surface is one security fix, W-SEC3, whose loopback binding, compose migration, dashboard forwarded-client check, doctor check and docs must ship together to close the LAN mint hole without stranding existing installs.
